body:
_Migrated from issue #1006, filed 2026-07-19._

Found while baselining the e2e suite for #855 (this reproduces on unmodified `main`, not on that branch).

`frontend/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` fails on most routes with the same violation:

```
Accessibility violations on grid/light:
  color-contrast [serious] — Elements must meet minimum color contrast
  ratio thresholds (31 node/s)
```

Affected in a single run: grid, book detail, edit book, smart shelf builder, admin, account, shelves, advanced-search, duplicates, reader, and the announcement banner — desktop and mobile.

## Notes

- It is **light-theme specific** (`grid/light`), which is why it isn't obvious day to day: the default palette is dark.
- Which route names appear varies run to run, because `theme.spec.ts` mutates the seeded user's persisted theme and the suite runs `fullyParallel`. The underlying contrast failure is stable; only its distribution shuffles.
- 31 nodes on a single page points at a **token-level** problem (a `--text-muted` / `--text-faint` / accent value in the `[data-theme="light"]` block of `styles/tokens.css`) rather than 31 separate component bugs.

## Why this matters

Per the project's a11y standard the gate is supposed to run with an **empty** known-violations list, so any critical/serious finding fails the build. Right now it is red nearly everywhere, which means it gates nothing — a genuinely new a11y regression would be indistinguishable from the existing noise.

## Suggested approach

1. Compute the actual contrast ratios for the light-theme text tokens against `--surface-1` / `--surface-2` / `--bg` and fix the failing token values (fixing the token likely clears most of the 31 nodes at once).
2. Re-run `npx playwright test a11y` on both themes until clean.
3. While here, consider making the theme-mutating specs restore the previous value (or run serially) so parallel runs stop reshuffling which routes report.

Related: #953 (the SPA e2e job is skipped on PRs, so none of this gates today).

resolution.note:
Duplicate of F-5647b8 (the a11y harness sampled colours mid theme-transition), fixed in #2053. NOT a light-palette defect, and the remedy this finding proposes would have made the product worse.

DISCRIMINATING EVIDENCE: every offending pair reported here crosses the two palettes, identified against cps-side styles/tokens.css:
  #9aa7b2 on #ffffff  = DARK --text-muted on LIGHT --surface-1
  #ece8e1 on #ffffff  = DARK --text       on LIGHT --surface-1
  #54606b on #1b2530  = LIGHT --text-muted on DARK --surface-1
  #23292f on #1b2530  = LIGHT --text       on DARK --surface-1
  #9aa7b2 on #e7e1d4  = DARK --text-muted on LIGHT --surface-3
No static cascade produces dark --text on light --surface-1 AND light --text on dark --surface-1 in the same scan; both directions together is the signature of axe reading an in-flight interpolation, with color and background-color crossing at independent times.

Within-light contrast passes AA comfortably: #23292f on #ffffff ~14.5:1, #54606b on #ffffff ~6.4:1. Darkening the light tokens as suggested would have shipped a worse palette to chase a number the harness invented, and the gate would then have gone green, confirming it.

MECHANISM: tokens.css --dur-fast is 120ms; a11y.spec.ts slept a fixed 250ms after flipping data-theme. A transition that starts late on a loaded runner still lands inside that window, which is why this reproduced reliably in July and is intermittent now. #2053 replaces the sleep with prefers-reduced-motion (global.css forces transition-duration 0.001ms !important) and asserts the preference actually reached the page.

CURRENT STATE OBSERVED, CI job 99287165128: 24 a11y tests passed, 0 failed, KNOWN allowlist empty, covering every route named here (grid, book detail, edit book, smart shelf builder, account, advanced-search, shelves, duplicates, admin, login unauthenticated, announcement).

title: [a11y] Light theme fails colour contrast on 31 nodes — the a11y gate is red across most pages
